summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted with persistent left-sided abdominal pain following a recent episode of peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis. Despite completing a week of intraperitoneal vancomycin and ceftazidime, her pain did not improve. Admission labs showed elevated peritoneal fluid white blood cells (730), supporting ongoing peritonitis, though cultures remained negative. A CT scan ruled out diverticulitis, showing only changes related to dialysis catheter use. She underwent peritoneal irrigation and continued antibiotics, with subsequent improvement in symptoms and a drop in peritoneal WBC to 14. Fungal and TB studies were negative, and fluconazole was discontinued. Her gastroparesis flared during admission, managed with domperidone and restarted metoclopramide with QTc monitoring. Diabetes was managed with adjusted insulin dosing. She completed a 10-day course of antibiotics and was discharged home with plans for follow-up in gastroenterology and nephrology.
problems: End stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis
Infection and inflammatory reaction due to peritoneal dialysis catheter
